turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Siobhan, I'll do your checks before Dr. O'Connell is in. Sleeve up there.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand. I'm wrecked, the bus was late, and I left the decent umbrella in the car. Typical, isn't it.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one hundred and eighteen over seventy-four, pulse ninety-two.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Is the pulse high? My sister's in the waiting room. She dragged me in, she's convinced I'm fading away.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): A touch quick, nothing wild. Oxygen ninety-eight percent, temperature thirty-six point seven, respirations sixteen.

[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): She was on at the desk, your sister. Heavy periods nearly two years, she said, and that you were breathless even sitting in the car. Thyroid trouble in the family as well, according to her.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah she would. I'm not breathless sitting down, that's pure drama. Stairs, yes. The periods are about a year, not two. And the thyroid is my aunt, not me.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello Siobhan, I'm Dr. O'Connell. Sorry for the wait. You've had the checks done, I see.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): We have. She's still outside on the phone. I told her I didn't need minding at forty-two, but sure look.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tell me what's brought you, in your own words.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm wrecked all the time, the periods are a disaster, I get puffed, and the hair is coming out. I cancelled the highlights because it'd only end up in the sink.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Start with the tiredness. How long has that been with you?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): The periods? Shocking. I keep a spare skirt in the drawer at work. I do the reception in the primary school, and the parents would have a field day if I leaked, you know yourself.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): The periods in a minute. The tiredness, how long?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Em, a good while. Same sort of time as the periods, I'd say. I'm all right early on and then I'm fit for nothing by half three.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the breathlessness, when do you actually notice it?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Two flights at the school and I'm catching myself at the top. On the flat I'm mostly grand. I'm not gasping sitting in this chair.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain with that?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really. It's the puffing. I wouldn't call it a pain.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Palpitations? The heart racing or skipping?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. That's her party piece, not mine.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): On the periods, you said about a year and she told the nurse nearer two. What do I put in the notes?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): A year. Last March, at my son's communion, I was mortified in the church. She was over in Birmingham, she wasn't even in the country, so she can stop correcting me.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): On a bad day, how many pads?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't count them, that's the honest answer. A good few. Maybe six, maybe eight, I lose track, and some nights I soak through to the sheet. It's a mess.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Clots at all?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, clots. About the size of a grape, or sometimes—
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bigger?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): A fifty cent piece, something like that, I can't be exact. Not every single time, but often enough that I've noticed.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): How many days, and is it still coming monthly?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): It was five days for years. Now it's more like eight or nine, with a trickle. Still roughly monthly. I haven't written it down, I keep meaning to.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bleeding between the periods, or after sex?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No between. Not after sex either. We're hardly ever at it with the tiredness, but when we are there's no bleeding.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any dizziness or fainting?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Lightheaded if I stand up too fast, a couple of times. I haven't fainted. I sat on the bottom step at home and it passed.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): The hair, then.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Coming out in the shower the last three or four months. No baldy patches, just thinner, and the drain is a disgrace.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cold? Weight going up or down? Constipation?

[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit cold in the hands, yeah. Weight, I think I've lost a bit, the jeans are looser, but I haven't stood on a scales so don't write it in stone. Bowels are grand, maybe sluggish, not constipated-constipated.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Swallowing all right? Any swelling in the neck?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): No and no. She prods my neck in the kitchen. There's nothing. It's all because of Auntie Nuala.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Go on about your aunt.

[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Mam's sister. Overactive thyroid, years back, and they removed it. Tablets for life after. I haven't the bulgy eyes or the shakes, so I don't buy that it's the same thing.
[SEG0044] person_1 (NURSE): I'll slip out in a second. Your sister said to put down that you take iron every day. Is that fair?

[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Every day? Not at all. Sometimes, when I remember, maybe twice a week if you're lucky. Brownish yokes, ferrous something, I forget the name on the box. Two hundred milligrams, or is it three hundred? I never actually look.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything else? Painkillers, the contraceptive pill, blood thinners?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Paracetamol, two tablets, when the cramps are bad. Not daily. No thinners. I came off the pill years ago after the second baby, and I'm not on it now.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any drug allergies?
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that I know of. Except penicillin, years ago, I got a rash. Or it was the bug I had, I couldn't tell you. I avoid it anyway, just in case.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): One of the infants asked me was I a granny yesterday. I'm forty-two. I nearly died. A granny, imagine.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the smoking?
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. Never. A glass of wine of a weekend, sometimes two, nothing in the week. I don't exercise either, the stairs don't count.
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Who's at home with you?
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Declan and the two boys, ten and seven. Herself is only over for the week, then Birmingham again. Great help, great torment.
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Headaches with any of this?
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Don't talk to me about the parking, I was circling twenty minutes and some lad in a jeep—
[SEG0058] person_1 (NURSE): Vitals are on the screen, doctor. I'll be just outside.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Headaches? No. Sorry, I was miles away there. No headaches.
[SEG0060] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any diabetes, asthma, heart disease, operations?
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): None of that. Two normal deliveries, no operations. I've been grand apart from this year.
[SEG0062] person_3 (DOCTOR): Up on the couch, and I'll examine you.
[SEG0063] person_2 (PATIENT): These shoes, she bought them, they're a death trap. Hang on.
[SEG0064] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pale in the face, and the inside of the lower lids is pale too. Heart sounds normal, regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No ankle swelling.
[SEG0065] person_3 (DOCTOR): Abdomen is soft, no tenderness, no mass that I can feel. I won't do an internal exam today.
[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): That's a relief. So what's the verdict, am I falling to bits?

[SEG0067] person_3 (DOCTOR): The picture that fits best is an iron deficiency anaemia driven by the heavy periods. It would explain the tiredness, the breathlessness on the stairs, the hair, and the pallor. I won't call it confirmed until we see the bloods.
[SEG0068] person_3 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't rule a thyroid problem out either, with your aunt, even if you don't sound classic. Better to test than to argue with your sister about it.
[SEG0069] person_2 (PATIENT): She'll love that. A proper test, not her poking me.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): Will I need to be fasting? I had a banana on the bus. And I hate needles, I went a bit funny at the dentist once, not an actual faint.
[SEG0071] person_3 (DOCTOR): No fasting. Full blood count, ferritin, and thyroid function, the nurse can take them after we finish. Banana is grand.

[SEG0072] person_3 (DOCTOR): For the iron, I want you on a set dose instead of whenever you remember. Ferrous sulphate two hundred milligrams once a day, with orange juice if you can, and not alongside the tea. I'll put it on a prescription.
[SEG0073] person_2 (PATIENT): Once a day, right. They bind me up, that's half the reason I let them slide. Is there a gentler one?

[SEG0074] person_3 (DOCTOR): This one first. If it truly doesn't suit, we can change it. Separately, if the bloods show you're anaemic, I'd want a pelvic ultrasound to look at the womb. Not booking it today, only if the bloods point that way.
[SEG0075] person_2 (PATIENT): A scan, grand. I've a school tour Thursday week I can't drop, the infants would riot.

[SEG0076] person_3 (DOCTOR): It won't be next week. Come back and see me in two weeks for the results either way, reception will slot you in. If you faint, or you soak a pad every hour, or you get a real chest pain, don't wait for me, go to emergency or ring the same day. And jot the pads down if you can, even a rough guess.

spec.situation: Tired, breathless woman with heavy periods for a year; counts pads and clots in vague terms; takes iron 'sometimes'; hair loss; relative mentions thyroid in the family. Blood tests, maybe pelvic scan.
features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: Sister via nurse alleged rest breathlessness; patient explicitly denies breathless sitting.
bad.text: breathlessness while sitting (category=respiratory, status=present, temporality=current, reported_by=nurse, certainty=disputed)

bad.reason: She denies true constipation but says bowels maybe sluggish.
No operations stated, but prior normal deliveries mean not absence of all prior procedures/events.
Conflict exists, but resolved by doctor documenting 'A year' per patient.

bad.reason: Conflict exists, but not unresolved; patient clearly denies breathlessness at rest.

omissions.text: Chest pain was effectively denied: patient said she would not call it pain, only puffing/breathlessness.
Heavy periods quantified as using about 6 to 8 pads on a bad day, with some nights soaking through to the sheet.
Menstrual clots were described as grape-sized and sometimes as large as a fifty-cent piece.
Periods used to last 5 days and now last 8 to 9 days with a trickle.
Hair loss detail: no bald patches, just overall thinning.
Bowels were described as 'maybe sluggish' despite not being constipated.
No internal/pelvic examination was performed today.
Patient reported ferrous tablets cause constipation/'bind me up', contributing to poor adherence.
Patient asked whether fasting was needed for the blood tests; doctor advised no fasting.
Patient has needle-related presyncope history: went a bit funny at the dentist once, but did not actually faint.

Symptoms of tiredness have a diurnal pattern: she is okay early on but 'fit for nothing' by about 3:30 pm.
